code: CASE(insn,ops) case insn: pc++; FETCH_ ## ops (); mrb->c->ci->pc = pc;
note: After fetching operands for each instruction, ci->pc is set to the current pc value. If this is the last instruction in the iseq, ci->pc points one past the end.
OP_SEND is executed; the CASE macro has already set ci->pc to point past the OP_SEND instruction. If OP_SEND is the final instruction, ci->pc now points to one past the end of the iseq.

code: ci = cipush(mrb, a, CINFO_DIRECT, NULL, NULL, BLK_PTR(blk), 0, c);
note: A new callinfo frame is pushed for the method call. The caller's ci->pc remains pointing one past the end of the caller's iseq.
The called method (a C function) is invoked. If this C function raises an exception, mrb->exc is set and control jumps to L_RAISE.
Exception detected after C method call; control transfers to the L_RAISE label for exception propagation.
During exception unwinding, the called frame is popped and the caller's ci->pc (pointing one past the end of the iseq) is restored into pc.
For backtrace generation, pc is set to ci->pc - 1. Since ci->pc points one past the end, pc points to the last valid instruction in the iseq.
idx is computed as the offset from the iseq start. Since pc points to the last instruction, idx equals irep->ilen - 1, which is within bounds.
This function is called with idx = irep->ilen - 1. The function checks if idx >= irep->ilen and returns FALSE without initializing loc.lineno and loc.filename, leaving them uninitialized.
loc.lineno is read after mrb_debug_get_position returned FALSE without initializing it. This is an uninitialized read vulnerability, as loc.lineno contains stack garbage.
loc.filename is also uninitialized and read here. If the garbage value happens to be non-NULL, it is used as a filename pointer, leading to potential invalid memory access.
